title: Making a plaster slump mould for air-dry clay
subtitle: Casting a simple plaster hump or slump mould from a found bowl or plate
excerpt: A plaster slump mould is made by pressing liquid plaster against the outside of an existing bowl or plate. Once set, the mould can be used to form consistent shallow dishes and platters in air-dry clay by draping a slab over the mould surface. One plaster mould produces hundreds of clay forms.
sourceNotes: Plaster slump mould technique derived from standard pottery practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: A convex or concave form over or into which a clay slab is draped or pressed to shape it
A fast-setting calcium sulphate powder mixed with water to form moulds; it absorbs moisture from clay to aid drying

content.text: allows you to make identical shallow dishes without a wheel. The plaster absorbs moisture from air-dry clay as it sits on the mould, helping the clay firm enough to hold its shape before it is removed. IMPORTANT: plaster contamination ruins a kiln-fired clay body. Keep all plaster tools and work surfaces completely separate from any clay destined for kiln firing.

materials.name: Found bowl or plate (the mould model, 15 to 25 cm diameter)
Air-dry clay (for using the finished mould)

content.text: Turn the model bowl upside down on a flat surface. Apply a thin coat of petroleum jelly over the outside surface and about 3 cm down the rim on the inside, to act as a release agent.

Mix the plaster: sift 500 g of plaster powder into 400 ml of cold water (never the reverse: always add powder to water). Stir slowly for 2 minutes until smooth. The plaster will begin to thicken at around 5 minutes.

Pour the plaster over the upturned bowl base and smooth it with a wet hand into an even layer at least 35 mm thick over the main surface. Allow the plaster to set: it will heat slightly as it sets. Wait 30 to 40 minutes before touching.

Once cool, carefully lift the plaster mould off the bowl model. Rinse the mould surface and allow it to dry at room temperature for at least 48 hours before using. A damp plaster mould does not absorb clay moisture effectively.
Using the mould with air-dry clay
Roll an air-dry clay slab to 6 mm thick. Place a sheet of thin cloth (muslin or tea towel) over the mould to prevent the clay sticking. Drape the slab over the top of the mould.

Smooth the slab down the sides of the mould with the sponge. Trim the rim level with the fettling knife. Allow to rest on the mould for 30 minutes, then lift off and place on a flat surface to finish drying.

items.problem: Clay dish sticks to the mould and will not lift off cleanly
items.cause: The clay was left on the mould too long and began to dry and contract onto the surface, or no cloth was used
items.fix: Always use a cloth layer between clay and mould. Remove the dish within 30 to 45 minutes while the clay is still slightly flexible. If stuck, gently insert a thin palette knife or card under one edge to break the seal

items.problem: Finished dish has a lumpy base
items.cause: Air bubbles were trapped in the plaster during mixing, leaving pits in the mould surface
items.fix: Fill surface pits in the mould with a small amount of fresh mixed plaster applied by finger and smooth once set. Mix plaster more slowly and avoid whisking to reduce air bubble formation
